Who it's for

Meditation and breathwork

The oil with the longest history of exactly this use, and still the most common reason people buy it.

Facial oil blends

Long used in skincare formulations, usually at one or two per cent in a carrier.

People who want one special bottle

If the rest of the range is everyday, this is the one most people treat as an occasion.

What people get wrong

Expecting church incense. That smell is frankincense resin burned on charcoal, which is a combustion product. The distilled oil is lighter, drier and faintly citrus, and people are often surprised by how different it is.

Buying the cheapest available. Frankincense is among the most commonly adulterated oils on the market, usually cut with cheaper resins or solvent residue. A low price is the most reliable warning sign there is.

What it won't do

There are several Boswellia species sold as frankincense — carterii, serrata, sacra, frereana — with genuinely different scents and prices. Ours is carterii. None of them are interchangeable.

Boswellia trees in parts of the range are under pressure from over-tapping. We buy small quantities and we would rather sell you less of it than more.

We describe how our oils smell and how people use them. We don't make medical claims, because essential oils aren't medicine.

Questions about Frankincense Quiet

Why does it not smell like incense?

Because incense is resin burning. Combustion creates smoky compounds that distillation does not. The oil is the lighter, drier, slightly citrus part of that smell, without the smoke.

Which Boswellia species is this?

Boswellia carterii. Serrata is the Indian species and smells sharper and more turpentine-like; sacra is closely related to carterii and often sold at a premium. The botanical name is the only way to tell them apart.

Is it sustainable?

Honestly, it is a concern across the industry. Over-tapping has damaged tree populations in parts of the growing range. We buy in small quantities from suppliers who can tell us where the resin came from, and we would rather be candid about this than claim certainty we do not have.

How long does it keep once opened?

Two to three years stored properly — cool, dark and tightly closed. Distilled oils keep considerably better than cold-pressed citrus.

What dilution should I use on skin?

Around 2% for the body — roughly 12 drops per 30 ml of carrier oil — and 1% for the face. Always patch-test before wider use, and never apply neat.

Can I take it internally?

No. None of our oils are food grade and none are sold for internal use. Essential oils are extremely concentrated, and advice to add them to water or food is not advice we endorse.

How quickly will it arrive?

Orders are dispatched from Delhi within two business days and usually arrive within a further three to five, depending on where you are. Shipping is free over ₹999.
